primary_claim: Sparse autoencoders trained on distance-embedded 2D point clouds learn features that correspond to a correct clustering of the data, following the rule 'a point is in cluster N if feature N activates on it'.

effect.value: median entropy ~0.1 (near-perfect) on basic_blobs/random_blobs baseline; 0.143 with adjoint clustering + tuned scale vs 0.326 default on random_blobs

stated_future_work: I have some real data to try this on next.
I haven't done enough baselining: do SAEs outperform DBSCAN?
Is the point cloud embedding "doing all the work"?
Find a reliable way to identify the correct number of features

limitations_stated: Not enough baselining against DBSCAN has been done
Method for finding the correct number of features (n_features) is not reliable
Encoder directions are far less interpretable than decoder directions
The approach has had less success with Anthropic-style SAEs, possibly requiring the k=1 sparsity constraint
quote: We find that the resulting SAE features are interpretable as a clustering algorithm via the natural rule "a point is in cluster N if feature N activates on it".
